review.finding: The replacement iterate-count command `grep -c '"type": "work_completed"' shipwright_events.jsonl` undercounts ~5x. The events writer switched to compact JSON separators partway through the file: this repo has 103 lines with `"type": "work_completed"` and 419 with `"type":"work_completed"` (522 total, all source=iterate). The prescribed command returns 103 and the gap widens with every new event, since all new rows use the compact form.
review.suggestion: Use `grep -c '"type": *"work_completed"' shipwright_events.jsonl` (matches both spacings) or `grep -c '"work_completed"'`; add a PowerShell equivalent alongside it, matching the new wc -c/wc -l PS block.
review.resolution: fixed: grep pattern changed to `'"type": *"work_completed"'` (verified: returns 522, matching both JSON formatting styles present in this repo's own event log).

review.finding: "this repo's own actual average is higher (several entries per iterate on a busy one), so in practice this repo crossed each line sooner" is derived from the undercounted iterate figure. review.suggestion: Reword to the measured direction (fewer than one decision entry per iterate on average, so the iterate-count column runs ahead of reality here) once the grep in line 29 is corrected; keep the 'trust the byte/line count' conclusion, which holds either way.
review.resolution: fixed: reworded to 'roughly two decision entries logged for every three finished iterates... needed more iterates than the iterate-count column implies to reach each line' (347/522 ~= 0.665, matches 2/3).
